paragraphs.title: God’s Honor and the Powerlessness of Idols

answers: To the idols
To the LORD’s name
To the makers of the idols
easy.explanation: The psalmist asks that glory be given unto the LORD’s name.
easy.q: To whom does the psalmist ask that glory be given?

answers: In the heavens
Among the idols
On earth only
easy.explanation: The KJV says, “our God is in the heavens.”
easy.q: Where is Israel’s God described as being?

answers: Stone and dust
Light and water
Silver and gold
easy.explanation: The idols are described as silver and gold, the work of men’s hands.
easy.q: What are the idols made of?

answers: They were made by human beings
They were created in heaven
They were formed by the LORD
medium.explanation: The phrase identifies the idols as human-made objects.
medium.q: In the KJV, what does “the work of men’s hands” mean?

answers: They are made by human hands and cannot function
They are located in the heavens
They are made only of gold
medium.explanation: Although they have bodily features, they cannot speak, see, hear, smell, handle, or walk.

answers: Their makers and trusters become like the powerless idols
Their makers become stronger than the idols
Their trusters become golden idols
medium.explanation: Verse 8 says, “They that make them are like unto them; so is every one that trusteth in them.”
medium.q: What connection does the psalm make between idols and those who make or trust in them?

answers: The LORD does whatever He pleases, while the idols are powerless
The LORD is made of silver, while the idols are made of gold
The LORD is on earth, while the idols are in heaven
challenge.explanation: The LORD has acted according to His will, whereas the idols cannot use their supposed senses or limbs.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast between the LORD and the idols?

answers: Because of the LORD’s mercy and truth
Because the psalmist does not know the idols
Because the idols demanded glory
challenge.explanation: Verse 1 grounds the request in the LORD’s mercy and truth.
challenge.q: Why does the psalmist ask that glory be given to the LORD’s name rather than to himself?

answers: People should not trust in powerless idols
People should trust idols when they are made of gold
Idols can act if they have bodily parts
challenge.explanation: The idols cannot speak, see, hear, smell, handle, or walk, so they are unworthy of trust.
challenge.q: What conclusion follows from the description of the idols?

paragraphs.title: The Call to Trust in God

answers: O Israel
The idols
The makers of the idols only
easy.explanation: The first command is addressed to Israel.
easy.q: To whom is the command “trust thou in the LORD” first addressed?

answers: The kings of the nations
They that fear the LORD
The makers of the idols
easy.explanation: Those who fear the LORD are also called to trust in Him.
easy.q: Who is mentioned alongside Israel and the house of Aaron?

answers: Their help and their shield
Their idol and their king
The heavens and the earth
easy.explanation: Each verse identifies the LORD as their help and shield.
easy.q: What is the LORD to each group called to trust in Him?

answers: He protects His people
He speaks for His people
He builds idols for His people
medium.explanation: A shield protects, so the verse presents the LORD as the protector of His people.
medium.q: In the KJV, what does “shield” communicate about the LORD?

answers: They all call people to trust in the LORD
They all describe the idols
They address only the house of Aaron
medium.explanation: Israel, the house of Aaron, and those who fear the LORD are each commanded to trust in Him.
medium.q: What do the three commands in these verses have in common?

answers: Because He is their help and their shield
Because He is made of silver
Because they do not live on earth
medium.explanation: The repeated reason is that the LORD is their help and shield.
medium.q: Why are Israel, the house of Aaron, and those who fear the LORD called to trust in Him?

answers: They may be presented as calls voiced by an outside speaker or congregation
Israel could not hear the commands
Israel was being identified as an idol
challenge.explanation: The wording “O Israel” presents an address from a speaker to Israel, possibly a leader or congregation.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the commands speaking of Israel in the third person?

answers: Israel, the house of Aaron, and they that fear the LORD
They that fear the LORD, the heathen, and Israel
The house of Aaron, the idols, and Israel
challenge.explanation: The three groups appear in that order in verses 9–11.
challenge.q: What is the order of the groups named in these verses?

answers: Trust is directed to the LORD rather than to idols
Trust is directed to silver and gold
There is no call to trust anyone
challenge.explanation: After exposing the weakness of idols, the psalm calls people to trust in the LORD.
challenge.q: How does the object of trust here differ from the subject of the preceding verses?

paragraphs.title: God’s Blessing upon Israel and Those Who Fear Him

answers: The house of Israel, the house of Aaron, and those who fear the LORD
Only the makers of idols
Only the great
easy.explanation: The verses name the house of Israel, the house of Aaron, and those who fear the LORD.
easy.q: Whom does the LORD bless in these verses?

answers: Only the small
Both small and great
Only the great
easy.q: Who is included in the blessing regarding age or status?

answers: The house of Aaron
Human beings
The LORD
easy.explanation: The LORD is identified as the One who made heaven and earth.
easy.q: Who is described as the Maker of heaven and earth?

answers: He will grant favor and blessing
He will make new idols
He will hide the heavens
medium.explanation: The repeated phrase expresses the LORD’s promise to bestow blessing.
medium.q: What does “he will bless” mean in this passage?

answers: Increase for the people and their children
More newly made idols
The lowering of heaven to earth
medium.explanation: Verse 14 says, “The LORD shall increase you more and more, you and your children.”
medium.q: What increase does the LORD promise?

answers: Verse 13 further identifies those whom the LORD will bless
Verse 13 cancels the blessing
Verse 13 changes to a description of idols
medium.explanation: After stating that the LORD will bless, the psalm specifies that those who fear Him, both small and great, will be blessed.
medium.q: How does verse 13 relate to verse 12?

answers: The certainty and breadth of the LORD’s blessing
The inability of the idols to speak
The limitation of the blessing to individuals
challenge.explanation: The repetition reinforces that the LORD will bless the different groups named.
challenge.q: What is emphasized by the repetition of “he will bless”?

answers: Only the house of Israel
The house of Israel, the house of Aaron, and those who fear the LORD, from small to great
Only the sons of Aaron
challenge.explanation: The verses include all three groups and both the small and the great.
challenge.q: What is the scope of the people receiving blessing?

answers: It presents Him as the source of blessing and as having power to bless
It teaches that the earth is made of silver
It limits the blessing to heaven
challenge.explanation: The Creator of heaven and earth is presented as the powerful source of blessing.
challenge.q: Why is the LORD’s identity as Maker of heaven and earth appropriate to this blessing?

paragraphs.title: The Heavens Belong to God and the Earth to Humanity

answers: To the children of men
To the LORD
To the idols
easy.explanation: The KJV says, “The heaven, even the heavens, are the LORD’s.”
easy.q: To whom do the heavens belong according to the psalm?

answers: To the children of men
To the idols
To the house of Aaron alone
easy.explanation: The earth has been given to the children of men.
easy.q: To whom has the earth been given?

answers: The dead only
The living, represented by “we”
The idols
easy.explanation: The psalm says, “we will bless the LORD,” referring to the living worshippers.
easy.q: Who is called to bless the LORD?

answers: People living on earth
The dead, who are described as entering silence
The makers of heaven
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the dead, who no longer participate in earthly praise.
medium.q: In the KJV, what are “they that go down into silence”?

answers: The heavens belong to the LORD, while the earth is given to humanity
The heavens belong to humanity, and the earth belongs to idols
The verses make no distinction between heaven and earth
medium.explanation: Verse 16 assigns the heavens to the LORD and the earth to the children of men.
medium.q: What distinction between heaven and earth appears in these verses?

answers: They are no longer among the living who can bless the LORD
They are living in the heavens
They are made of silver
medium.explanation: Verse 17 says that the dead do not praise the LORD.
medium.q: Why can the dead not fulfill the call to praise in these verses?

answers: The dead do not praise the LORD, but the living will bless Him
The dead praise Him, but the living remain silent
The heavens praise Him, but the earth does not exist
challenge.explanation: Verse 17 excludes the dead from praise, while verse 18 commits the living to bless the LORD.
challenge.q: What contrast is made between verses 17 and 18?

answers: For a short time only
Beginning now and continuing forever
Only while the heavens are visible
challenge.explanation: The phrase expresses continual praise beginning in the present and lasting forever.
challenge.q: What does “from this time forth and for evermore” mean?

answers: Since the earth is given to humanity, the living on it are called to bless the LORD
The earth prevents people from blessing the LORD
The earth is an idol that cannot hear
challenge.explanation: The earth is the human sphere, and the living people in it are called to praise the LORD.
challenge.q: How is the earth connected with the call to praise?
